DESIGN AND EVALUATION OF INFRAGUARD AI
Governance-by-Design Reference Framework for
Bounded LLM-Assisted Incident Triage

PROJECT DEFENCE
Adebodun Samuel Tomola  |  2025/A/MIT/0616
Supervisor: Dr. Emmanuel Mkpojiogu
Miva Open University  |  August 2026
textPreview: DESIGN AND EVALUATION OF INFRAGUARD AI | Governance-by-Design Reference Framework for | Bounded LLM-Assisted Incident Triage |  | PROJECT...

text:
Open with the bounded thesis: InfraGuard AI proposes and instantiates a governance-by-design reference framework for bounded LLM-assisted incident triage.
The condition-and-ruleset fingerprint is the distinctive implemented construct. The artefact is not evidence of autonomous or production-ready incident response.

[Sources]
- InfraGuard_AI_Masters_Project_REVISED_AFTER_28_AUGUST_REVIEW.docx, title page, Abstract and Sections 6.2 to 6.4
[/Sources]

name: Google Shape;89;g3ba14ccda94_0_28
text:
• Knowledge — reliability of a compact local model remains uncertain
• Design — governance must be embedded in evidence, memory and action boundaries
• Engineering — small teams need an inspectable operator-hosted reference artefact
• Empirical — cross-model, workload, cost and production evidence remain limited

Design-science contribution — governance-by-design reference framework
Distinctive construct — condition-and-ruleset acknowledgement fingerprint
textPreview: • Knowledge — reliability of a compact local model remains uncertain | • Design — governance must be embedded in evidence, memory and act...

text:
Separate the four gaps before describing novelty. The project does not claim a new foundation model.
The scoped originality is the combined governance-by-design framework, not invention of AI governance or alert acknowledgement in general.
The fingerprint is the framework's distinctive implemented construct; the feature comparison does not establish universal novelty or superiority.

[Sources]
- InfraGuard_AI_Masters_Project_REVISED_AFTER_28_AUGUST_REVIEW.docx, Sections 1.2.1, 2.1.8, 2.4.5 and 6.3
[/Sources]

name: Google Shape;89;g3ba14ccda94_0_28
text:
• Automation bias can produce misuse, disuse or complacency
• Trust should be calibrated to demonstrated reliability and visible evidence
• Alert fatigue makes repeated presentation—not inference—an operational concern
• Human-AI guidance requires capability disclosure, correction and user control
• Organisational AI governance requires accountable roles, controls and evidence
• Trustworthy AI turns principles into continuing risk and monitoring duties

Design implication — structured output never replaces operator judgement
textPreview: • Automation bias can produce misuse, disuse or complacency | • Trust should be calibrated to demonstrated reliability and visible eviden...

text:
Theoretical foundations are Design Science, organisational AI governance, trustworthy AI and appropriate reliance. Observability, SRE, AIOps and RAG are domain concepts; bounded context, provenance, validation, acknowledgement and approval are design constructs.
Alert fatigue is a motivation, not a measured outcome in this study.

[Sources]
- InfraGuard_AI_Masters_Project_REVISED_AFTER_28_AUGUST_REVIEW.docx, Sections 2.1.6 to 2.1.8 and 2.4.5
- Mäntymäki et al. (2022); Morley et al. (2020); NIST (2023, 2024); Raji et al. (2020); Lee and See (2004)
[/Sources]

• RQ4a — implementation evidence and qwen2.5:3b behaviour
• RQ4b — descriptive perceived usability in the evaluated group
• RQ4c — unresolved diagnostic, cross-model, cost, workload and field claims
• RQ5 — security, deployment and data-governance constraints

text:
The overarching design contribution is the governance-by-design framework; this fingerprint is its distinctive implemented construct and its main identity limitation.
The 30-cycle figure is deterministic: later warning rows are masked from the default view, while all 30 model calls and records remain.
The same model can supply the signature used for acknowledgement, creating circularity. Deterministic telemetry-derived identity is the recommended next design.

[Sources]
- InfraGuard_AI_Masters_Project_REVISED_AFTER_28_AUGUST_REVIEW.docx, Sections 2.1.8, 2.2.4, 3.4.5, 4.2.5, 5.3 and 5.6.2.2

textPreview: CRITICAL PRECISION  •  27.3% | recall and precision tell different safety stories

text:
This is exact agreement with the frozen four-class labels for qwen2.5:3b, not a universal score or chance comparison.
C20 sensitivity does not rescue the result: an acceptable {ok, warning} set remains 29/72 because all three predictions were critical; excluding C20 gives 29/69 only as a post-hoc sensitivity result.
Under-calls may delay response; repeated over-calls may increase review burden and erode calibrated trust.

name: Google Shape;89;g3ba14ccda94_0_28
text:
Design science — governance-by-design reference framework for bounded LLM-assisted triage
Distinctive construct — condition-and-ruleset fingerprint with severity safeguard
Engineering — inspectable operator-hosted implementation and reproducible evidence package
Empirical — reproducible baseline exposes retrieval strength and severity/signature weakness
Human evidence — exploratory two-assessor interpretation and descriptive SUS in ten complete responses

Defensible conclusion — provides inspectable decision-support functionality; does not establish improved decisions, workload reduction, autonomous triage or production effectiveness

Next evidence — deterministic signatures, stronger models, live workloads and larger independent human studies
textPreview: Design science — governance-by-design reference framework for bounded LLM-assisted triage | Distinctive construct — condition-and-ruleset...

text:
Close on the bounded hierarchy: governance-by-design framework, fingerprint construct, reference implementation and configuration-specific empirical findings.
Do not claim workload reduction, production certification, commercial superiority or autonomous remediation.

[Sources]
- InfraGuard_AI_Masters_Project_REVISED_AFTER_28_AUGUST_REVIEW.docx, Sections 6.2 to 6.4 and Table 5.12
[/Sources]
